principle: Templated processes that GUIDE a frontier LLM through capability synthesis WITHOUT letting it jump down a branch too fast: at every stage it must enumerate options before committing, prefer deterministic over model, test before descending, troubleshoot before backtracking, and TRACK DATA at every step. The LLM proposes within these rails; the scaffold + tests + governance dispose. Used by _repos/teleon/backend/src/teleon/synthesis/intent_to_dag.frontier_prompts(). serves_truth=false.

discipline.say: List >=3 candidate components for the step WITH tradeoffs before choosing one. Do not commit on the first idea.
Never pick a model/LLM rung while a deterministic tool (parser/rules/classifier/solver) could meet the bar. Justify every escalation to a model.
Stay at the current level until its options are compared + the chosen one is TESTED. Do not deepen the DAG on an untested assumption.
Define + run a test for each component in isolation before building anything on top of it.
On a failure, run the troubleshooting ladder (diagnose -> isolate -> try alternative) BEFORE abandoning the branch.
Record for every node: the options considered, the choice + why, the test result + actual output, cost, latency, confidence.
Climb every wired rung before reporting unavailable; then name the next cataloged rung. Never give up at rung 0.
Each modification is ONE versioned branch; keep the losers with lineage so you can jump back up and try another.

stages.goal: understand the goal + context before proposing how
stages.prompt: Restate the goal, the constraints, and the given context in your own words. Then list 2-3 candidate APPROACHES at a high level with their tradeoffs. DO NOT pick one yet and DO NOT write components. Prefer approaches that lean on cheap deterministic methods.
avoid: jumping straight to an LLM-does-everything plan

stages.goal: choose the cheapest component that meets the bar, per step
stages.prompt: For EACH outline step, list >=3 candidate components from the registries (DETERMINISTIC first), each with cost / latency / license / determinism / governance. Pick the cheapest that can meet the bar and JUSTIFY. If you pick a model, state which deterministic options you ruled out and why.
avoid: picking a model when a parser/classifier/solver exists

stages.goal: build the DAG and test every node before relying on it
stages.prompt: Assemble the chosen components into a DAG. For EACH node define a concrete test + expected output, run it in isolation, and record pass/fail + the ACTUAL output + cost + latency. Only after a node passes may a downstream node depend on it. Then test the whole DAG end-to-end.

For each node, group, and the whole DAG, answer the 5W1H ladder: WHO produces/consumes it; WHAT it asserts (deterministic?); WHERE each value comes from (provenance); WHEN it was computed + does it go stale (CDC); WHY this rung over cheaper/dearer; HOW it is verified + how it fails HONESTLY (MISSING, not fabricated).

For the chosen path (each node + the groups), name >=2 alternatives and their pros/cons (cost, latency, license, determinism, governance). Explicitly ask: could a DETERMINISTIC tool replace this model rung? Is there a cheaper path that still meets the bar? Recommend keep-or-switch with reasons.
avoid: defending the first choice without alternatives

troubleshooting_ladder.do: re-run the failing node with the recorded input; confirm the failure is real + deterministic
pin the failure to a single node (not its inputs/downstream)
category: component-bug | wrong-component-for-the-data | missing-dep-or-key | data/format-issue | bar-too-high
if component-bug / missing-dep-or-key / data-issue: fix config/input + re-test (no branch change)
if wrong-component: swap to the next same-plane alternative (a new versioned branch) + re-test
if no same-plane alternative works: jump back up to the parent decision + try its next branch
if the whole rung can't meet the bar: climb to the next (dearer) rung; record why the cheaper rung failed
if every wired rung is exhausted: report unavailable honestly + name the next cataloged rung. Never fabricate.
